why_it_matters: G-hs3 was the last structural obstacle on the strip band above the frontier: hs3 = |W_n| + |K - (P_n - I_n)| < floStripMin at a hypothetical off-pair zero. Discovery 0117 closed G-hs3-i (the EM/W-side term is dominated by the on-line B-wire). This closes the K-side: the P6 finite-kernel deviation-ratio family (the Mr wire) is evaluated at the off-line kernel, where the g-product carries g^(-sigma) factors at sigma = 1/2 +/- d0 that the on-line wire never evaluates. The lift uses the SAME classical 1.6 convexity bound the tree already cites on the line, transferred through the functional equation - the worst side is sigma = 1/2 + d0 (exponent 1/4 + d0/2), and the b3 correction is sigma-independent (S4Strip.X4fun has no sigma input), so the off-line wire keeps the on-line M * e^X * X shape at the lifted mass. Every machine part is LEAN-proven on the band with exact-decimal pins (margin ~16 orders at the corner). Consequence: on the strip band above the Platt-Trudgian frontier, the endpoint hs3 leg reduces, by t4m_Bupper + t4m_Bmono + t4m_resid_strip, to hW (cited zero-free record + T4OffD, all CITED records, no analytic input) + hK (ONE cited convexity mass). hs3 is now body-provable above the frontier and should drop out of the RHEnd stripfront premises.

Then the residual endpoint faces are hs1 (G-hs1, the S1 uniformity face) and hWin (zero-exclusion above the cited frontier, the record-shadow face) - both CITED-record faces, not analytic barriers.
